test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In Jainism, who is a Tirthankara?

options.text: A saviour and spiritual teacher of the dharma who teaches the way to moksha, or liberation.
A person who believes in one God and one spirit and believes in rebirth.
A person who never believes in God.

solution:
The correct answer is: __** A saviour and spiritual teacher of the dharma who teaches the way to moksha, or liberation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tirthankaras **__are spiritual leaders in** Jainism who have achieved enlightenment**
 
• They have helped others to** achieve the same by establishing the principles of Jainism** and showing the** path to liberation**
 
• __**Tirthankaras **__are believed to be** human beings who have attained a state of perfection** and have become free from the cycle of birth and death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Tirthankaras **are considered to be the **embodiment of compassion and non-violence.**
 
• **Jains believe that there have been 24 Tirthankaras** in the current cosmic age.
 
• Each Tirthankara has a unique emblem and symbol that represents them, such as **a lion, elephant, and so on.**
 
• **Tirthankaras are believed to have attained enlightenment** through their own efforts and not through any external help.
 
• **Tirthankaras are not considered as gods**, but rather as role models for Jains to follow t**o achieve spiritual liberation.**
 
• Jains believe that by following the teachings of Tirthankaras, one can attain the ultimate **goal of Jainism, which is liberation from the cycle of birth and death.**
